1	# SMA-860: capture a zero-argument tool-call stream for five conformance subjects
2	
3	- **Linear:** SMA-860 (follow-up of SMA-567)
4	- **Date:** 2026-11-24
5	- **Branch:** `feature/sma-860-capture-a-zero-argument-tool-call-stream-for`
6	
7	## 1. Intent
8	
9	SMA-567 added the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` scenario to the stream conformance suite
10	(`tests/provider-stream-conformance`). Only `openai/responses` serves it. Five subjects are pinned
11	in the `UNCAPTURED` table with SMA-860 as the follow-up: `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`,
12	`litellm` and `openai/chat`.
13	
14	The suite accepts a fixture only if it meets the provenance rule (`CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format
15	fixtures"). So each of the five subjects needs a real capture before it can serve the scenario.
16	This change commits the five captures, serves the scenario from them, and removes the five rows.
17	
18	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
19	
20	**Goals.**
21	
22	- G1. Each of the five subjects serves `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from a committed capture.
23	- G2. Each committed capture is byte-identical to the wire, and its provenance is recorded.
24	- G3. A test fails when a script's copied payloads differ from the committed capture.
25	- G4. The five `UNCAPTURED` rows for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` are removed.
26	- G5. The design records what each provider actually sends for a zero-argument call. The ticket
27	  asks for this, in particular for a stream with no argument deltas and for the Gemini `null`
28	  arguments.
29	
30	**Non-goals.**
31	
32	- No change to a provider translator, unless the suite finds a conformance failure (SMA-533
33	  design §9 applies). §5 predicts that no failure occurs.
34	- No change to the `ReasoningCleanStop` rows (SMA-858) or the `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` rows
35	  (SMA-859).
36	- No new scenario and no translator fix for a stream with truly zero argument deltas. No capture
37	  shows one (§4). §6.7 files a follow-up instead.
38	
39	**Anti-goals.**
40	
41	- A capture that is labelled CAPTURED but has an edit that nothing records.
42	- A script that "fixes" a capture so that it matches a sibling subject.
43	
44	## 3. Approach
45	
46	Three approaches were considered:
47	
48	- **A. Commit a fixture file and copy its payloads into `conformance.rs`.** This is the
49	  `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` pattern of the `openai/responses` subject (SMA-567). The SMA-567 design (§6.9)
50	  requires it. Its risk is drift between the copy and the file.
51	- **B. Commit a fixture file and `include_str!` it from the script.** No drift can occur. But this
52	  adds a new serving pattern and a frame parser for each wire format.
53	- **C. Record the capture only in the module doc** (the Gemini "Live capture" pattern). This is the
54	  weakest provenance, because doc comments usually elide values.
55	
56	**Sven picked A** on 2026-11-24. The spec challenge showed that review alone does not stop drift:
57	the anthropic, gemini and litellm drivers skip an unparseable `data:` payload with only a
58	`tracing::warn!`, so a copy error can drop a frame and still pass every floor. So this design keeps
59	A for serving and adds one guard test for each subject that compares the consts with the committed
60	file (§6.3). The guard reads the file, but the script does not.
61	
62	## 4. The captures
63	
64	Claude ran the captures on 2026-11-24 with Sven's keys and the AWS profile `maip-dev-admin`, at
65	Sven's request. Each request offered one tool, `get_current_time`, with the description "Return
66	the current server time. Takes no arguments." and the user message "What time is it?". Each
67	request forced the tool call. Request headers (keys) are not recorded.
68	
69	| Subject | Endpoint | Model | Time (UTC) | Argument deltas on the wire |
70	|---|---|---|---|---|
71	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:38:59 | One `input_json_delta` with `partial_json: ""`. `content_block_start` carries `"input":{}`. |
72	| `openai/chat` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `gpt-5-mini` (wire: `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`) | 20:39:21 | The first `tool_calls` delta has `arguments: ""`. One more delta has `arguments: "{}"`. |
73	| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | 21:14:44 | No deltas. One `functionCall` part with `"args": {}`. |
74	| `bedrock` | `https://bedrock-runtime.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/model/eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5/converse-stream`, sent with `curl --aws-sigv4` | inference profile `eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:39:45 | One `contentBlockDelta` with `toolUse.input: ""`. |
75	| `litellm` | LiteLLM 1.98.0 proxy (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm@sha256:3a1980074ff2ac13883e0ffee1bebec345d8addd004be251079cee173b0e8305`, the SMA-547 digest), `/v1/chat/completions` | proxy alias `zero-arg-anthropic` (the wire `model` value), upstream `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:59:06 | Three `tool_calls` deltas: `""`, `""`, `"{}"`. |
76	
77	The committed files (§6.1) are the bytes as received. Their sizes and SHA-256:
78	
79	| Subject | Bytes | SHA-256 |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| `anthropic` | 1364 | `b6114d956d7d80a6b315fcd2f6866fff8c776e9ebbed846c8ab7ccf9093dd86e` |
82	| `openai/chat` | 1618 | `5c5e74ac372aa0f954e89801c0addb62592a1ae02ad3c36b427b4d24f56d8cf2` |
83	| `gemini` | 1383 | `45271e2e2c96d08f183bec5251811498fee18b74c3cbfc92f9a2fc7c35542624` |
84	| `bedrock` (binary) | 1250 | `9196618e83783e261b5a3997d81a8cb343ff58bb1c560bff611a53c0d6a98b04` |
85	| `litellm` | 1739 | `b81bc790cdcf6a93e1ef6e8391a353a344d95549ef08a412ee0f7c1f241552c7` |
86	
87	Check with `shasum -a 256 tests/provider-stream-conformance/fixtures/*/zero_arg_tool_call.raw`.
88	
89	**Findings.**
90	
91	1. **No provider sent a stream with truly zero argument deltas.** Anthropic and Bedrock send one
92	   delta with an empty string. So the accumulated arguments text is `""`, not `{}`. Gemini sends
93	   the whole call in one part. A zero-delta stream still has no capture for any subject.
94	2. **The `anthropic` and `bedrock` translators depend on that empty delta.** Both emit the tool
95	   name only with the first input delta (anthropic `src/stream.rs` near 173-193, bedrock
96	   `src/stream.rs` near 196-219). On a stream with no input delta they emit no `ToolCallDelta` but
97	   still emit `Finish(ToolCalls)`. `openai/chat` and `litellm` have `flush_buffered_names` for this
98	   shape, and `openai/responses` has the SMA-562 synthesis. §6.7 files a follow-up.
99	3. **Gemini sent `"args": {}`, not a missing `args`.** The `"null"` path in
100	   `providers-gemini/src/sse.rs` did not occur. An earlier Gemini capture at 20:39:23 declared the
101	   tool with no `parameters` field. The SDK never sends that (`translate/tools.rs` always sends
102	   `parameters`), so it was captured again at 21:14:44 with `{"type":"object","properties":{}}`.
103	   Both captures show the same shape. Only the second one is committed.
104	4. **Gemini ends each SSE line with CRLF.** The other four text captures use LF. The existing
105	   `.gitattributes` rule `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/*.sse text
106	   eol=lf` would change these bytes. So the committed file has the `binary` attribute (§6.1).
107	   `parallel_signed.sse` (SMA-827) is LF in git. The record does not show whether its wire was
108	   CRLF.
109	5. **LiteLLM emits `""`, `""`, `"{}"` for an Anthropic upstream.** The direct Anthropic capture
110	   (20:38:59) sent one `""`. The LiteLLM run made a different upstream call, which nobody captured.
111	   So "LiteLLM adds the `{}`" is an inference, not an observation.
112	6. **Bedrock sends `messageStop` before `metadata`.** This is the first recorded Bedrock order:
113	   `messageStart`, `contentBlockStart`, `contentBlockDelta`, `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop`,
114	   `metadata`. The `toolUse` start carries `"type":"tool_use"`, and `metadata.usage` carries
115	   `serverToolUsage:{}`.
116	7. **Each capture has fields that the translators do not use.** Examples: `caller` (Anthropic,
117	   LiteLLM), `p` padding (Bedrock), `obfuscation` (OpenAI), `inference_geo`, and spaces before the
118	   closing `}` on five Anthropic `data:` lines. The scripts keep them, because a CAPTURED payload
119	   is sent byte for byte.
120	
121	## 5. Expected suite behaviour
122	
123	The spec challenge traced each shape through the current translators:
124	
125	- `anthropic` ignores `content_block_start.input` and `caller`. The empty `input_json_delta` emits
126	  the name with `""`. `ping` is a no-op.
127	- `bedrock`: the `input: ""` delta emits the name. The SDK skips `p` and `serverToolUsage`.
128	- `gemini`: `args {}` becomes `"{}"`. A bare EOF runs `finish()`. `STOP` after a `functionCall`
129	  gives `ToolCalls`. `eventsource-stream` accepts CRLF.
130	- `litellm`: chunk 1 buffers the name, chunk 2 flushes it with `""`, chunk 3 adds `{}`.
131	- `openai/chat`: async-openai 0.43 knows `obfuscation`.
132	
133	The `ToolCallsMismatch` floor (`src/lib.rs` near line 1032) and assertion 10 (`src/check.rs` near
134	line 192) both read blank arguments as `{}`. So the `""` arguments of `anthropic` and `bedrock`
135	match the declared call `get_current_time` with `{}`. No translator change is expected. If a
136	subject fails, the builder stops, records the failure, and treats it as a SMA-533 §9 finding. The
137	builder does not edit the capture to make it pass.

- **Linear:** SMA-860 (follow-up of SMA-567)
- **Date:** 2026-11-24
- **Branch:** `feature/sma-860-capture-a-zero-argument-tool-call-stream-for`

## 1. Intent

SMA-567 added the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` scenario to the stream conformance suite
(`tests/provider-stream-conformance`). Only `openai/responses` serves it. Five subjects are pinned
in the `UNCAPTURED` table with SMA-860 as the follow-up: `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`,
`litellm` and `openai/chat`.

The suite accepts a fixture only if it meets the provenance rule (`CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format
fixtures"). So each of the five subjects needs a real capture before it can serve the scenario.
This change commits the five captures, serves the scenario from them, and removes the five rows.

## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals

**Goals.**

- G1. Each of the five subjects serves `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from a committed capture.
- G2. Each committed capture is byte-identical to the wire, and its provenance is recorded.
- G3. A test fails when a script's copied payloads differ from the committed capture.
- G4. The five `UNCAPTURED` rows for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` are removed.
- G5. The design records what each provider actually sends for a zero-argument call. The ticket
  asks for this, in particular for a stream with no argument deltas and for the Gemini `null`
  arguments.

**Non-goals.**

- No change to a provider translator, unless the suite finds a conformance failure (SMA-533
  design §9 applies). §5 predicts that no failure occurs.
- No change to the `ReasoningCleanStop` rows (SMA-858) or the `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` rows
  (SMA-859).
- No new scenario and no translator fix for a stream with truly zero argument deltas. No capture
  shows one (§4). §6.7 files a follow-up instead.

**Anti-goals.**

- A capture that is labelled CAPTURED but has an edit that nothing records.
- A script that "fixes" a capture so that it matches a sibling subject.

## 3. Approach

Three approaches were considered:

- **A. Commit a fixture file and copy its payloads into `conformance.rs`.** This is the
  `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` pattern of the `openai/responses` subject (SMA-567). The SMA-567 design (§6.9)
  requires it. Its risk is drift between the copy and the file.
- **B. Commit a fixture file and `include_str!` it from the script.** No drift can occur. But this
  adds a new serving pattern and a frame parser for each wire format.
- **C. Record the capture only in the module doc** (the Gemini "Live capture" pattern). This is the
  weakest provenance, because doc comments usually elide values.

**Sven picked A** on 2026-11-24. The spec challenge showed that review alone does not stop drift:
the anthropic, gemini and litellm drivers skip an unparseable `data:` payload with only a
`tracing::warn!`, so a copy error can drop a frame and still pass every floor. So this design keeps
A for serving and adds one guard test for each subject that compares the consts with the committed
file (§6.3). The guard reads the file, but the script does not.

## 4. The captures

Sven's request. Each request offered one tool, `get_current_time`, with the description "Return
the current server time. Takes no arguments." and the user message "What time is it?". Each
request forced the tool call. Request headers (keys) are not recorded.

201-
202-A wire-format fixture is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends. A reader must know which bytes are real and which bytes are not. Five rules apply.
203-
204-SMA-585 shows the risk. `responses_tool_call.txt` is a CAPTURED fixture, but the file ended with a `[DONE]` line that the Responses endpoint does not send. The header did not record the line.
205-

## SMA-860 final whole-branch review (base 87953869, head cac015a9)

I read the full diff, the spec, the ledger and CONTRIBUTING "Wire-format fixtures", and I checked the five `.raw` files directly. I changed no file and moved no git state.

What I ran:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance --all-features`: 85 lib tests and 20 integration tests pass. This includes the five guards, `blank_args_match_a_declared_empty_object` and the three `eventstream` tests.
- `cargo clippy -p … --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p …`: clean.
- markdownlint: clean. The two `docs/superpowers` files are excluded by the config.
- I did not run the full workspace test or the doc-coverage script.

### Strengths
- **Spec §4 values match all five guard docs and the files.** I checked sizes and SHA-256 with `shasum`: 1364/b6114d…, 1618/5c5e74…, 1383/45271e…, 1250/919661…, 1739/b81bc7…. Times, endpoints and models also agree between the spec, the arm comments and the guard docs.
- **The guards are stronger than spec §6.3 asks.** Each SSE guard compares the concatenated script output with the whole `.raw` file. So a payload byte, a frame boundary, CRLF or LF, or a missing or extra frame each fails the guard. The bedrock guard decodes the file and also decodes the script output. This differs from the spec's "split the file and compare with the const through one shared helper". It is a justified improvement, and the plan's pre-flight scan recorded it.
- **The capture claims are true against the bytes.** I decoded `bedrock/zero_arg_tool_call.raw` myself:
  - It has six frames in the stated order.
  - The capture header order is `:event-type`, `:content-type`, `:message-type`, as the arm comment records.
  - The Gemini file has CRLF (4 CRLF pairs). The other three SSE files are LF only.
  - The Anthropic capture has spaces before `}` on five lines.
- **`.gitattributes` is correct.** `git check-attr` shows `binary` on all five `.raw` files. `git ls-files --eol` shows `i/crlf` for the Gemini file and `-text` for bedrock. The index blobs equal `hash-object --no-filters` of the working files. So no filter changed the bytes, and a Windows checkout cannot change them either. The consts in `conformance.rs` contain no literal newlines, so a CRLF checkout of the `.rs` file cannot change them.
- **No test now checks nothing.** `uncaptured_rows_name_only_allow_listed_scenarios` still iterates the rows that remain. The mock tests keep their single purpose. `encodes_stop_reason` is still checked by the harness for each served scenario (`src/lib.rs:417`).
- **The mutation evidence is recorded.** The bedrock report has (a) `ToolCallsMismatch`, (b) a guard failure and (c) `InsufficientEvidence`, "no ToolCallDelta". This confirms SMA-863.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important
1. **Two module provenance lists are now false or incomplete.** Spec §6.5 named only the gemini list, so the plan missed these two.
   - `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2150-2156` (anthropic): "The CAPTURED fixtures that this module copies from are the three SMA-840 captures". This is now false, because the module also copies `fixtures/anthropic/zero_arg_tool_call.raw` byte for byte.
   - `conformance.rs:1468-1470` (litellm): "Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a fixture committed in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/`". The list does not include the new capture under `tests/provider-stream-conformance/fixtures/litellm/`.
   - This matters because these lists are the CONTRIBUTING rule 1 and 5 provenance records, and that record is the purpose of this ticket. Gemini, bedrock and openai_chat have the new capture in their lists. Anthropic and litellm do not.
   - Fix: add one bullet to each list, in the form of the gemini bullet at `:3348-3351`. In the anthropic list, change "the three SMA-840 captures" to include the zero-argument capture.
   - Must fix before merge: yes. It is doc only and takes about four lines.

#### Minor
1. **`conformance.rs:279-281` (bedrock `script()` doc) is false for the captured scenario.** It says "Each script is the same Converse stream cut at a different point". The zero-argument script is a different, captured stream with a different tool and different ids. The ledger deferred this item. Recommend: fix before merge, because it is a one-line doc fix.
2. **`conformance.rs:103-105` (bedrock module doc) is imprecise.** "The suite decodes the file and encodes the frames again with `frame_raw`" suggests that the served frames come from the file. In fact the script encodes the `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` consts, and only the guard decodes the file (spec §3: "The guard reads the file, but the script does not."). Suggest: "The script encodes `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` with `frame_raw`, and the guard decodes the file and compares." This is optional.
3. **The spec §6.1 provenance record names "the request file", but three guard docs omit it.** The anthropic (`:3298-3308`), gemini (`:4162-4171`) and bedrock (`:765-777` area) guard docs do not name `zero_arg_tool_call.request.json`. Litellm gives only the directory. Only openai_chat names the file. CONTRIBUTING rule 1 does not require the request file, so this is a deviation from the spec only. It is optional but cheap.
4. **Four gemini doc sentences have a stale count.** "Both recorded … captures" appears at `conformance.rs:3449`, `:3592`, `:3674` and `:4008`. There are now three Gemini captures. Each claim is still true for the new capture (usage on every chunk, bare `data:` frames, a whole `functionCall` in one chunk, `"STOP"` after a call). Only the word "both" is stale. This is optional.
5. **The bedrock guard doc says "Changed: nothing".** Its arm records a header reorder under "Edits made here". This is consistent, because the record is about the file and the guard doc says that the suite encodes the frames again. A reader can still misread it. This is optional.

### Ledger triage (must it be fixed before merge?)
- T1, the lib test asserts only "no `ToolCallsMismatch`": no. It matches the brief, and a stronger `is_none()` is optional.
- T2, redundant closure: no. Clippy is clean.
- T3, no positive marker control in the litellm scan test: no. The harness checks `encodes_stop_reason` against `fixture_finish_reason` for each served scenario (`src/lib.rs:417`), so it already covers this.
- T4, stale `declines.rs` comment: already fixed in T6. I checked that the comment is gone.
- T6 Important, `:79-80` "each shape comes from those two sources": fixed and verified. It is now scoped to the hand-authored scenarios.
- T6, `script()` doc "same Converse stream cut at a different point": recommend fixing before merge (Minor 1).
- T6, `every_bedrock_script_keeps_message_stop_before_metadata` should assert that `checked` contains ZeroArg: no. The zero-argument script is already checked, because `script()` returns `Some` for it. Pinning it is optional.
- T6, long doc line `:188`: no. It is cosmetic, and fmt is clean.
- T7, trybuild ruling: I agree that it is out of scope. The branch touches no `crates/` file (`git diff --stat` over `crates` is empty), and `publish = false` is set. So release-plz releases nothing.
- T7 Important, null `finish_reason` docs at `:824-826` and `:940-942`: fixed and verified. They are now true: chunks 0 and 1 carry `"finish_reason":null`, and the capture has no text content delta.

### Recommendations
- Fix Important 1 and Minor 1 in one `test(providers): SMA-860 …` commit. Then re-run `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` and fmt.
- Put the §6.9 mutation results for each subject in the PR body. For anthropic and bedrock, include the empty-delta removal result: `InsufficientEvidence`, "no ToolCallDelta".

### Declined to judge
- The user message "What is the weather in Berlin?" in each zero-argument `request()`. The captured requests used "What time is it?". The mock server does not read the request, and spec §6.2 requires only the tool and the forced choice to match.
- Whether real ids (`msg_…`, `chatcmpl-…`, `toolu_…`, the Gemini `thoughtSignature`, `responseId`) may stay in the committed captures. Spec §6.1 decided this: the suite crate is unpublished.
- The `.request.json` and `litellm_config.yaml` files have no eol attribute, so a Windows checkout can convert them to CRLF. No code reads them, and no doc claims that they are byte-exact.
- The full-workspace CI gates (all-crate test, doc-coverage, Windows and macOS legs). I ran only the suite crate gates, and the branch touches no other crate.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge: with fixes.** These are doc-only fixes: Important 1, and Minor 1 is recommended.

**Reasoning:** The captures, the guards, the table and mock changes, and `.gitattributes` are correct and byte-exact on every platform. The suite gates are green. The one Important finding is a false provenance sentence in the anthropic module and an incomplete list in the litellm module, which the spec's §6.5 sweep did not list.
